findings.title: Wrapped enabled state can suppress required login-cache invalidation
findings.description:
`update()` obtains `original` through `getById()`, whose organization-aware wrapper reports disabled when the organization is disabled. If a previously cached public IDP becomes private during that period, both predicates return false and invalidation is skipped. Re-enabling the organization leaves the private IDP in login results: organization updates do not invalidate these login caches, and the login bean only rechecks `isEnabled()`.

Compare persisted IDP eligibility rather than organization-dependent enabled state, and add a regression covering public-to-private updates while the organization is disabled.

findings.title: Cleanup targets a literal alias instead of created providers
findings.description: The cleanup here and at line 425 removes `"alias"`, not the created `idp-alias-*` provider. `TestCleanup.executeCleanup()` executes these callbacks without catching `NotFoundException`, so teardown can fail immediately and leave fixtures behind. Register the actual aliases, accounting for the provider explicitly removed during the test.
